title: Moving fire survivors off FEMA interim housing
summary: As of August 31, the County is meeting with FEMA on how caseworkers can meet together with residents at the Kīlohana housing site, and an official said not everyone living there will be eligible to stay. A clinician said patients worry FEMA will make them leave at month's end. The site is moving from a federal to a county facility, and more than 1,100 households remain in temporary housing, with the gap lasting until 2030.

timeline.text: Maui Now reported that Maui County will take ownership of the 167-unit Kīlohana modular housing project, which could become permanent housing.

source.quote: Maui County will take ownership of the 167-unit Kīlohana modular housing project, now serving Lahaina wildfire survivors, in a move that could pave the way for the temporary homes to become permanent housing, County Council members learned Wednesday.

timeline.text: A new rental help program, the Disaster Interim Housing Program, starts in August.

timeline.text: FEMA temporary housing assistance for Maui wildfire survivors was extended to February 2027, which is context for the clinician's concern about residents being made to leave at month's end.

source.publisher: Office of the Governor, State of Hawaiʻi
source.quote: U.S. Department of Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem has approved Hawaiʻi's request to extend FEMA Temporary Housing Assistance for Maui wildfire survivors until February 2027, providing critical stability for individuals and families still recovering from the August 2023 wildfires.
